description: A small Node project with one declared script SURE can turn into a check, and no authorisation to run it. The project is not defective and it is not being asked to be: the case is what a report must do with a check that could not be carried out. The trap is a report that quietly drops it — a reader then sees a headline, a capability line and `No unresolved findings.`, and takes the silence for a pass on the one thing SURE could not do.

read_by.route: the plan holds one entry whose decision is `Denied` (`sure_domain::execution::decide` refused `ActionKind::RunTests` under `InspectOnly`), so `not_run` produces a `CheckResult` whose status is `Skipped` and whose `not_checked_reason` is `NotCheckedReason::ExecutionNotAuthorized`
read_by.returns: one skipped result carrying the frozen sentence, which reaches the reader through `ProjectVerdict::not_checked`, through `Aggregate::coverage.critical_not_checked`, through `CoverageNotCheckedSummary::not_checked`, through the `cannot_confirm` finding `sure_core::findings_from_checks` raises for it into `ProjectVerdict::findings`, and through the two lines `render_summary` prints

project.declared_script: "test": "node src/totals.test.js", which is what `npm test` runs
project.dynamic_check: the `test` script becomes one check: `chk_nodetestd6032c00e4d44f94`, titled `run the tests`, severity `must_fix`, critical
project.project_file: `sure.yaml` asks `execution: mode: host_confirmed`. It is a request and not a grant: `Layer::can_grant` refuses a project file, so the run still plans under `inspect_only` and the request is left behind as a refused escalation. The fixture ships it so that a build which read execution authority out of the project would be a red test rather than an undetected escalation.

execution_refusal.why_no_goal: The run supplies no goal, the way `sure check` runs with no `--goal`. That is why the rendered summary carries the after-the-fact caveat as well as the count of checks that could not run; both lines are asserted, so neither can be dropped.

Unresolved findings: 1 Must fix.
4 check(s) could not run or were skipped. 2 of them are critical. (run the tests, build the project)

moved.from: not there: the user has granted nothing, so the plan refuses the check
moved.to: one file under a configuration root this test owns, saying `execution: mode: host_confirmed`
moved.how: `Paths::from_roots` puts SURE's configuration root under `target/tmp` for the length of the test, `Authority::load` reads it together with the fixture's own `sure.yaml`, and `Authority::execution()` is the pair `sure check` hands the pipeline. The machine's real configuration directory is never read and never written.

file.why: the whole of what the user's own file says, and the same line `sure check` reads. The file is written rather than a literal being handed to the pipeline, so the route from a person's decision to the run's permissions is the one the product actually has.

moved.keys_are: the two answer blocks compared key by key, sorted. The test reads the difference off the declarations and compares it with this list, so a control that stopped moving something, or started moving something else, is a red test rather than a change nobody noticed.

control.why: The same project, the same `package.json`, the same planned check and the same pipeline run, with the user's own file the only thing that appeared. Standard `sure check` reads execution authority from that file alone, so this is not a test-only route: it is the route — with one boundary this declaration has to state rather than gloss, and which `P18-T007` is what put there. The runner this test hands the pipeline is `ProcessRunner::new` over a `Cancellation` the harness cancels before the run begins. That is the product's own runner and a real cancellation, and `crate::process::run` checks it before it spawns, so this half can carry an authorised check all the way to the runner without starting `node` on the machine that grades it. What a real `sure check` on a real machine would then do with this check is therefore **not measured here at all**: what is measured is that the check is no longer refused, that it reaches the runner, and what the product says when the runner answers. A reporter hard-wired to deny — the failure this fixture exists to catch — would satisfy every positive assertion above and fails here, because the refusal must be gone when the user has granted it.
control.unchanged: The project's own `sure.yaml` still asks for `host_confirmed` in both runs and is still only a request in both: what moves is the user's file. The keys the two declarations share that say what did *not* move are the summary lines (the same six, line for line), the check's identity and weight, the count of checks that could not run, the finding the run raises for that check — one `must_fix` `cannot_confirm` finding anchored to it on both sides, because consent decides what SURE may do and not what SURE knows — and the aggregate's headline and severity, which are `not_enough_checked` either way, because the check is unanswered in both runs: refused in one, errored before it started in the other, and neither is a check that was carried out. Consent changes what SURE is allowed to do; it does not make anything checked, and since `P7-T012` it does not change what SURE says about the project either. The one key that moved when `P18-T007` wired the pipeline to the runner, beyond the ones this control was written for, is `critical_not_checked`: a refused check is a critical check that was not checked, and a check that errored before it started is a critical check that errored, so the aggregate routes it into `critical_errored` instead. Both are `not_enough_checked`; the route is what moved, and it is named in `moved.keys` rather than left to be discovered. **`P18-T011` added a third kind of row to both sides and changed not one entry of `moved.keys`.** The same three roles `package.json` does not declare are rows of both runs, so `not_checked_count` is four on both sides and the summary lines are still the same six, line for line, closing with the same sentence; the addendum to the outcome above about the aggregate's counts holds here word for word. The two keys this control already declared as moving — `coverage_skipped` and `aggregate_skipped` — now move from four to three rather than from one to zero, because the refused check becomes the errored one while the three declarations stay skipped; `coverage_could_not_run` still moves from zero to one and `critical_not_checked` still empties, exactly as declared. A key that was not moving before is not moving now, which is why the list this control's `moved.keys` holds is unchanged rather than widened.

required_outcomes.why: The acceptance sentence is *dynamic-not-authorized stays visible*, and every word of it is asserted by equality against SURE's own answer rather than paraphrased. `check_status` is `skipped` and `check_not_checked_reason` is `execution_not_authorized` — the frozen vocabulary has no "not authorized" status at all, so a build that invented one would fail here. `check_reason` is the whole sentence `crates/sure-domain/src/status.rs` fixes for that reason, quoted rather than searched for. Visibility is asserted in five places rather than one, because a struct field is not a report: the result is in `ProjectVerdict::not_checked`, it is in `Aggregate::coverage.critical_not_checked`, it is an entry in `CoverageNotCheckedSummary::not_checked`, the run raises one `cannot_confirm` finding for it into `ProjectVerdict::findings` (added by `P7-T012`, and the five keys at the end of this entry pin its weight, its status and the check it is anchored to), and the last two lines of the rendered summary name it and count it. `coverage_checked` is zero, which is the honest half a reader could otherwise miss: nothing was checked at all, and the check is neither a pass nor a failure. The project's own `sure.yaml` asking for `host_confirmed` is asserted beside it — `project_ask_refused_escalation` is true, `project_ask_granted` is false — because a build that took execution authority from the project would have made this answer a green light on a stranger's advice. **`P18-T011` moved four of the numbers in this block and left every verdict in it alone, and the movement is recorded rather than left to be discovered.** The declarations a manifest cannot make used to be handed to the aggregate as results and land in its `unscheduled` field, which no renderer reads — the row existed and the report did not hold it. They are now handed to `aggregate_run` as rows of the run, so the three roles `package.json` does not declare — `build the project`, `check the code for style and likely mistakes`, `check the types without building` — are counted beside the check that was refused: `not_checked_count`, `coverage_skipped` and `aggregate_skipped` are four rather than one, and the last summary line is *4 check(s) could not run or were skipped. 2 of them are critical. (run the tests, build the project)*. What the fixture exists to assert did not move: all three are `Skipped` with `NotApplicable` and `blocks_green` false, so the critical build row is in `critical_out_of_scope` rather than in `critical_not_checked`, `blocking` still holds the refused check alone, the aggregate is still `not_enough_checked`, the run still raises exactly the one `cannot_confirm` finding anchored to the refused check, and `is_ready_for_hand_off` is still false. The count of checks that could not run is now the count of rows the run holds, which for a project with one script and three undeclared roles is four.

required_outcomes.why: The fixture is worth nothing without this half, and the assertion that makes it a measurement is the negative one: with the user's own file granting execution, **no result carries `ExecutionNotAuthorized`** — asserted by that predicate, not by a count of passes and not by a greener aggregate. `refusals` is declared as zero and the test computes it as `results().iter().filter(|result| result.not_checked_reason == Some(NotCheckedReason::ExecutionNotAuthorized)).count()`, so a reporter that refused everything fails here and a reporter that refused nothing fails the outcome above. What the check becomes is stated rather than dressed up, and `P18-T007` is the task that re-made this half: `crates/sure-core/src/pipeline.rs` is wired to `planned_check_runner`, so a check the user's file allows is handed to the runner the harness gives the pipeline and the answer here is that runner's — `check_status` is `error` with `check_reason` *the run was cancelled before the command was started, so nothing ran*. That runner is `ProcessRunner::new` over a `Cancellation` the harness cancels before the run begins, so the check is carried to the real runner and the runner provably starts nothing; without that, grading this fixture would start `node`. What a real `sure check` would do with this check is therefore not measured here, and that is a boundary rather than a result. `coverage_checked` stays zero — an error is not a check that ran — and the aggregate stays `not_enough_checked`, now through `critical_errored` rather than `critical_not_checked`, which is why `critical_not_checked` is one of the keys this control declares as moving. The honest reading of this half is still "the reason changed", not "the project got greener", and the sentence that used to say *if a later build learns to carry the check out, this declaration is what has to be re-made* is this re-making: the build did, and this is what changed. **`P18-T011` moved this block's counts the way the outcome above records, and for the same reason:** `not_checked_count` is four and `coverage_skipped` and `aggregate_skipped` are three, because the three roles this manifest does not declare are rows of the run on both halves rather than rows only the refused half held. The negative assertion this half is measured by — that no result carries `ExecutionNotAuthorized` — is untouched by that, and it is still the assertion that decides the control.

forbidden_outcomes.description: The check that nobody authorised is missing from the report, so the run reads as a project with nothing outstanding. A plan entry that was refused and a plan entry that passed must never look the same to a reader, and `No unresolved findings.` on its own is exactly that mistake.

The project is reported as ready to hand off, as passing, or as verified. The one thing in this project SURE would have had to run to say anything about is the thing it was not allowed to run, so any sentence of that kind is a green light on an unread check.

The lack of authorisation is reported as a defect in the project: a failure, a `must_fix` that says the code is wrong, a finding whose status is `open` rather than `cannot_confirm`, or an outcome that names the code as the thing to fix. Nothing here is wrong — the script is declared and the file it names exists — and a project must not be blamed for a permission the person at the keyboard has not given. This sentence used to forbid the finding itself, in the words 'a finding, a failure, or a `must_fix` about the code', and `P7-T012` made that half false: a check the plan refused is a material uncertainty a reader has to be told about, and `sure_core::findings_from_checks` raises one `cannot_confirm` finding for it, carrying the check's own `must_fix` rather than a weight chosen for the project. What survives is the distinction the sentence was written for, and the test asserts it rather than leaving it to a reader: the finding's status is `cannot_confirm` and never `open`, what it says is that SURE planned this check and did not run it, its impact is that nothing here is known to be broken, and its next step is to run the check or to allow SURE to run it — never to change the code.

The project's own `sure.yaml` is treated as authorisation. A repository SURE was merely pointed at cannot decide that SURE may run it, which is the escalation `docs/architecture/CONFIG_AUTHORITY.md` exists to prevent; a build that read the mode from the project would show this check as allowed.

notes: `dynamic-not-authorized` is a case in `evaluation/acceptance-manifest.json` with `release_blocking: false`, `expected_severity: "note"` and the expectation `unexecuted dynamic checks stay visible as not checked/skipped`; the two fields at the top of this file are copied from that row rather than chosen here, and `every_fixture_agrees_with_the_manifest_about_id_severity_and_blocking` in `crates/sure-testkit/tests/fixture_apps.rs` fails if either drifts. The row is why this fixture is **not** in `FIXTURES_WITHOUT_A_MANIFEST_CASE`: it has a case, and the exemption list is checked in both directions. SURE reports one `Finding` for this case since `P7-T012`, and this sentence is where that is written down: the refused check is a plan entry that reported nothing, and `sure_core::findings_from_checks` raises one `cannot_confirm` finding for it carrying the check's own `must_fix`. This sentence used to say SURE reports no `Finding` for this case, which that change made false — and the reason it is worth saying rather than leaving out is that it is the exact sentence the forbidden outcome below used to be written against. What it still says is unchanged: the `must_fix` the check itself carries is the weight of the check, not a candidate about the project, `candidates.material` and `candidates.style_noise` are both empty, and the case's `expected_severity` of `note` is the manifest's row for what SURE says about the project rather than the weight of a check nobody authorised. The test asserts the buckets rather than leaving them to a reader. This is the second fixture in the corpus that ships a `package.json` without being one of `P14-T001`'s scanners, so it is named in `TYPESCRIPT_FIXTURES` for the reason that file gives — a directory that ships a `package.json` is a Node application and belongs in the runnability sweep — and the test that grades it lives in `crates/sure-core/tests/adversarial_fixture_detection.rs`, where the real pipeline is reachable. The pipeline is driven with `store: None`, so grading this fixture writes nothing anywhere, and the project is read where it ships rather than copied, so a fixture edited without the test being edited is a red test.
